hyps.why: Without the direct 0->3 edge, removing 2->3 often cuts most or all input-output paths, so the drop is much larger.
If 2->3 is already absent, removing 0->3 leaves only edge 4 feeding the output, which risks disconnection and starves the output node.
With 2->3 absent, edge 4 is one of only two output inputs, so deleting it removes a large share of the cell's computation.
If 0->2 is absent, removing 0->1 leaves nodes 1 and 2 with no input, collapsing the cell to the single edge 3.
If 0->1 is absent, edge 1 is node 2's only source of signal, so deleting it kills both intermediate nodes.
When 0->2 is absent, node 2 depends entirely on 1->2, so removing it disables edge 5's contribution.
Replacing a missing edge with a 3x3 conv restores a path and adds capacity, a larger gain than swapping out an existing op.
Average pooling on the direct output edge is among the worst choices, so replacing it with a conv gains more than replacing skip or conv1x1.
A residual skip on 0->3 is most useful when a deep conv path through node 2 exists, forming the ResNet-like pattern found in top cells.
When 2->3 is absent, edge 4 is a main computational route to the output, so making it a 3x3 conv adds disproportionately more.
